clue.text: Cite question before election with leader deposed

indicators.note: before places the question abbreviation ahead of the trimmed election word
the leader of a word is its first letter, and deposing it removes that letter

parts.note: an election is decided by a vote

explanation.surface: Someone is quoting a question asked ahead of a poll in which the party leader was ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: VOTE with its first letter removed leaves OTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite a source is to repeat its words, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Artist with conservationists below feature of college is part of a circle

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces placed below come after the first piece

parts.note: a quad is the quadrangle courtyard found at many colleges
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: An artist and some heritage campaigners pose beneath a college building, said to be part of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter of a circle, bounded by two radii and an arc, is a geometry term for this shape.

clue.text: Unusual description of sick policeman?

definitions.meaning: a police officer who is ill is off sick, away from the patrol area, or beat

explanation.definitionFit: Something unconventional is called off-centre or eccentric; read in two words it also describes a constable away from the patrol route.

clue.text: Island hotel bankrupted? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, so the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A hotel on an island is asked whether it has gone bust, and the reply is not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of hotel and the start of bankrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island where Napoleon was first exiled is a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Loathsome quality in lecturer detained by eccentric genius and son

indicators.note: being detained by means being held inside, so the lecturer letter goes within the rearranged letters
eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters of genius are rearranged

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A lecturer finds himself held captive by a mad genius and his son, a hateful situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' turns GENIUS into UGINES; 'detained by' puts L inside to give UGLINES, then S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hideous or repellent is the quality the abstract noun names.

clue.text: Serious measure requiring change in unpopular work period

parts.note: grave means solemn or serious
a yard is an imperial measure of length
to shift is to change or move

explanation.surface: A grave step requiring alteration, set within a disliked period of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The overnight work stint, unpopular because of its antisocial hours, has this idiomatic name.

clue.text: Sacred bird is in the same place first

indicators.note: first puts the footnote abbreviation at the front of the answer

parts.note: IB is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place, used in footnotes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holy bird and something else found in the same spot first.
explanation.definitionFit: The wading bird was held sacred in ancient Egypt, linked to the god Thoth.

clue.text: Model European with religious book

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, religious
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A European model posing with a religious book.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect example of something is its model, a synonym in the sense of ideal type.

clue.text: In New York, fine snappily-dressed person

definitions.meaning: Americans use the word as an adjective meaning excellent or great
a dandy or fashionably dressed man about town

explanation.definitionFit: The word is American slang for excellent and also an old term for a dashing, smartly turned-out gentleman.

clue.text: Legislative official arrests magnate in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parliamentary officer arrests a tycoon who has got himself into difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer keeps order in a legislature such as the House of Commons, and can make arrests there.

clue.text: Friendly fellow found in a story

indicators.note: found in says the fellow letter is located inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: A friendly chap turns up in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Being genial and easy to talk to is what friendly describes, a synonym.

clue.text: Foolish mistake made in road to Tyneside?

indicators.note: made in says the mistake is placed within the road

parts.note: the A1 is the main road up the east of England, written with I for the digit one
a sin is a wrong or error
NE is the north-east of England, where Tyneside lies and where the A1 heads

explanation.surface: A silly error is made on the main road up to Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 runs from London to the North East, so 'road to Tyneside' suggests A1 then NE, with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or stupid, literally donkey-like, a synonym.

clue.text: Bank not imposing a charge first to last

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the last position

parts.note: free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A bank that charges no fees moves from first to last.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of rock or coral just below the sea surface is this ridge.

clue.text: Sanction in a European country church disowned

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: disowned means rejected, so the church letters are taken out

parts.note: Greece is a country in southern Europe
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A European nation gives approval after disowning its church.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction a plan is to consent to it, a synonym.

clue.text: Pass around ball for fan

indicators.note: around means the pass word is wrapped about the ball

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A footballer passes the ball round for a supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan something is to make it less hot by moving air, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A set having little weight in study

indicators.note: in places the small weight inside the study

parts.note: a den is a private study
oz, an ounce, is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A set of things weighing very little is kept in the study.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of twelve items is a common set, as eggs are sold.

clue.text: Chair is briefly fixed by hammer, say

parts.note: is shortened to an apostrophe S
a hammer is an example of a tool

explanation.surface: A chair is quickly mended with a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A backless seat is a type of chair, a loose synonym by example.

clue.text: Animal that none moved — source of pride to a people?

definitions.text: source of pride to a people?

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal that nobody had moved becomes a nation's pride.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's official patriotic song is sung with pride by its people.

clue.text: Wear ties incorrectly in a kind of way

indicators.note: wearing something incorrectly suggests the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone wears neckties the wrong way, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means so to speak or in a manner, a hedging idiom.

clue.text: Miscreant moved wrongly signs in text

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are placed in an incorrect arrangement

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer moved mistakenly, as signs in a text show.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks are punctuation signs used in written text.

clue.text: Province associated with Spice Girl, say, and a country

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province
Geri Halliwell was one of the Spice Girls, a 1990s British pop group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A province linked with a pop singer, and a country.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African nation is a country, the definition naming its category.

clue.text: Wine and nuts I consumed in time

parts.note: nuts means crazy

indicators.note: consumed in means eaten up inside, so I goes within the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wine and nuts that I ate in a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from the Portuguese island of the same name.

clue.text: Attendant's element in book

definitions.meaning: a boy servant attending a knight or noble
one leaf side of a book

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a young servant at court and one sheet side of a book.

clue.text: Type of muscle associated with a Northern nut

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of muscle is linked with a nut from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is an edible nut from a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: Malicious bachelor exiting — creating a nasty sensation?

indicators.note: exiting means leaving, so the bachelor letter goes

parts.note: bitchy means spiteful or malicious

explanation.surface: A spiteful bachelor leaves, causing an unpleasant feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes you want to scratch causes an irritating, unpleasant sensation on the skin.

clue.text: Correct woman missing hospital

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the hospital letter is dropped

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A woman missing from hospital is put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text by fixing errors is to correct it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Jogger's first set of exercises includes a source of light relief?

indicators.note: includes means the other pieces hold the A inside them
first means only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: PE is physical education, a school exercise class
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner's opening workout includes something to laugh at.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank or practical joke provides some fun and light relief.

clue.text: By the sound of it, section in church in cut-off location

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver to go by how a word is pronounced

parts.note: an aisle is a passage or side section of a church

explanation.surface: A part of a church seems, from what is heard, to be in a remote place.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a place cut off from the mainland by water.

clue.text: Surprised expression shown by gentleman harbouring a criminal at sea

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so the A goes within the gentleman word

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentleman, to cries of astonishment, shelters an outlaw at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate or privateer is a criminal operating at sea, as the Barbary raiders were.

clue.text: Celebratory time in Florida, say, with figure getting about

indicators.note: getting about means going around, so the number word surrounds the time

parts.note: five is a figure, a number
EST is Eastern Standard Time, the time zone of Florida, for example

explanation.surface: In Florida, a figure travels around at a celebratory time.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive means cheerful and suited to a celebration, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Settle around region in the Arab world?

indicators.note: around means the settle word is placed on both sides of the region

parts.note: to nest is to settle in a place
an area is a region

explanation.surface: People settle around a region of the Arab world.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of south-west Asia including the Arab countries is traditionally given this geographic name.

clue.text: Remove from roster a sentry

indicators.note: from here means taken out of the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: A guard is struck off the duty list.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across roster, a and sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to remove or delete it, a synonym.
